title: SRE Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines Redwood Inference's SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning methodology, reliability initiative lifecycle, incident review requirements, operational tooling expectations, and canonical runbook structure. It is intended for SREs, oncall engineers, service owners, and platform/product stakeholders.

Scope:
Applies to all externally visible inference services (hosted API, dedicated API endpoints) and critical internal subsystems (control-plane, billing, routing, KV cache). For private deployments, customers may adopt these standards as recommended baseline.

Key contacts / owners:
- SRE Lead: Ari Chen (engineering)
- Platform Owner: Maya Patel (engineering)
- Production Support: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai

1) Definitions and Principles
- SLO: quantified target for availability or latency for a single service or route.
- Error budget: 1 - SLO (allowed unreliability over a rolling window).
- SLI: observable metric used to measure SLO (e.g., successful requests, p95 latency).
- Rolling window: default 30 days for availability SLOs, 7 days for latency where applicable.
- Primary principle: keep SLOs simple, measurable, actionable; prioritize customer experience and cost-effectiveness.

2) SLO taxonomy and templates
All services MUST define at least one availability SLO and one performance SLO if latency materially affects UX. Use the templates below when creating new services.

Availability SLO (template):
- SLI: successful request rate (HTTP 2xx within ingress timeout)
- Window: 30d rolling
- Target: 99.95% (hosted API default) OR service-specific (see table)
- Measurement: ingress ELB + API gateway combined success ratio (exclude scheduled maintenance windows)
- Owner: service oncall

Performance SLO (template):
- SLI: p95 inference latency (end-to-end request -> last token emitted)
- Window: 7d rolling
- Target examples:
  - Routing & gateway: p95 < 100ms
  - Small model endpoints (<= 1B params): p95 < 200ms
  - Medium model endpoints (1B-15B): p95 < 450ms
  - Large model endpoints (>15B): p95 < 1200ms
- Measurement: synthetic + production sampled traces via X-Ray/Jaeger and metric aggregation in Grafana/Prometheus

SLO examples table:
| Service | SLO (availability) | Latency SLO (p95) | Rolling window | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| hosted-api-default | 99.95% | p95 < 300ms | 30d / 7d | api-team | applies to public /generate endpoints |
| inference-runtime | 99.9% | p95 < 600ms | 30d / 7d | runtime-team | includes model load/eviction |
| control-plane | 99.99% | n/a | 30d | infra-team | RPC for job management |

3) Error budget policy and operational playbook
- Calculate error budget as (1 - SLO) * window. Track budget burn daily.
- Burn thresholds and required actions:
  - Green (burn < 25% of period budget): normal ops, schedule improvements in backlog.
  - Yellow (25% <= burn < 50%): investigate root causes, prioritize fixes in next milestone.
  - Orange (50% <= burn < 80%): require weekly reliability check-in with owner + SRE to plan mitigations.
  - Red (burn >= 80%): immediate mitigation plan required; reduce feature launches, enable hardened routing policies, consider temporary throttles.
- Automated mitigations (when available):
  - Auto-failover to standby region/model-variant when latency/availability breaches thresholds.
  - Degraded-mode responses: shorter max tokens, reduced parallelism, disable expensive features (e.g., large context retrieval).
- Governance: If a service reaches Red twice in a 90-day period, a Reliability Initiative (see section 4) must be opened and staffed.

4) Capacity planning and sizing standards
Goals: ensure headroom for 99th-percentile load spikes, maintain error budget targets, and control cost.

Forecasting cadence:
- Weekly short-term (1 week): SRE & Platform run capacity checks based on rolling usage metrics and upcoming scheduled events.
- Monthly medium-term (1-3 months): Product + SRE produce capacity forecast for expected growth & planned sales/partnerships.
- Quarterly long-term (3-12 months): Exec-level planning for new regions, large sales commitments, Dedicated capacity offers.

Capacity model (summary):
- Inputs: qps by route, average tokens per request, p95 latency target, batching efficiency factor, KV cache hit-rate, model throughput (tokens/sec/GPU).
- Headroom rules: maintain >= 40% spare GPU capacity (reserve) for hosted API; dedicated pools can use lower reserve based on commit.
- Throttle policies: set request-level soft limits at 85% of provisioned capacity to trigger autoscaling / queueing.

Example sizing calculation (simple):
1. Measured p95 throughput: model A = 120 tokens/sec/GPU at target latency.
2. Expected sustained tokens/sec = mean qps * mean tokens/request.
3. Required GPUs = ceil((expected sustained tokens/sec / model throughput) * (1 + safety_margin)).
Safety_margin default = 0.4 (40%). Document calculations in the service capacity worksheet.

Capacity runbook checklist (weekly):
1. Confirm autoscaling events and failures in past 7 days.
2. Verify GPU utilization per cluster (target avg 35%-60%).
3. Validate queue lengths and request rejection rates.
4. Confirm cache hit rates >= 70% for high-throughput workloads.
5. Produce snapshot and escalate anomalies.

5) Reliability initiatives lifecycle
When to open an initiative:
- Postmortem identifies systemic causes that require engineering work (not ops playbook edits).
- Service hits Red error budget twice in 90 days.
- Forecast indicates capacity shortfall for committed customer deliveries.

Initiative template (required fields):
- Title, description, owner, start date, target completion, success criteria (SLO improvement, cost delta), milestone plan, stakeholders, QA/rollback risks.
- Track in eng-platform/roadmap board and tag as reliability.

Review cadence:
- Weekly working group for active initiatives.
- Monthly exec review for multi-quarter initiatives.

6) Incident review and postmortem standards
All Sev >= 2 incidents must have a postmortem published within 7 business days. Postmortem MUST include:
- Incident summary (timeline, impact, duration, root cause)
- Alerting & detection timeline
- Mitigations applied and timeline
- Root cause analysis (5 whys / causal chain)
- Contributing factors and systemic findings
- Action items (owner, due date, verification steps)
- Error budget impact and whether burn thresholds were crossed
- Follow-up reliability initiative if applicable

Postmortem public template (use Confluence page):
1) Title: YYYY-MM-DD Sev X: Short description
2) Summary: Who, what, when, impact (customers affected, p50/p95 impacts, % requests failed)
3) Timeline: minute-level for first 60 minutes, then 5-15m granularity
4) Root cause and analysis
5) Corrective actions (what fixed) + Preventative actions (what will change)
6) Verification & closure criteria
7) Lessons learned and metrics to validate improvement

Sev classification quick guide:
- Sev 1: System-wide customer impacting > 6 hours or major region outage
- Sev 2: Customer-impacting degradation affecting > 5% requests or key customers degraded
- Sev 3: Functional degradation affecting a subset or internal tooling

7) Operational tooling & observability requirements
Minimum stack for any SRE-monitored service:
- Metrics: Prometheus (service metrics, e.g., request_success_count, request_latency_seconds_bucket)
- Traces: OpenTelemetry -> Jaeger/X-Ray for distributed traces
- Logs: Structured logs to LogQL / Elastic with request_id correlation
- Alerts: Alertmanager / PagerDuty integration with runbook links and playbook IDs
- Dashboards: Grafana per-service + per-team overview panels (SLO panel, capacity, errors, latencies)

Recommended alerts (examples):
- Availability alert: if (5m_success_rate < 99.5% AND 30m_success_rate < 99.7%) -> page SRE oncall
- Latency alert: if (p95_latency > SLO_target * 1.5 for 10m) -> notify service owner
- Capacity alert: if (GPU_utilization_avg > 85% for 15m) -> page platform oncall

Example PromQL for availability (Prometheus):
- success_rate_5m = (sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))) * 100

8) Runbook standards and canonical runbook (structure)
Every runbook must be a Confluence page under eng-sre/runbooks and include the following flat sections:
- Title and short description
- Scope and impact
- Ownership and escalation path (names and PagerDuty IDs)
- Preconditions and required credentials (links to vault paths)
- Detection & symptoms (how the issue manifests in metrics/logs)
- Immediate mitigation steps (ordered, numbered)
- Root cause diagnostics (commands, log locations, queries)
- Recovery steps and verification
- Post-incident notes and follow-up tasks

Canonical example: inference-runtime-degraded-runbook
- Scope: inference-runtime (model inference workers, KV cache, router)
- Symptoms: p95 latency spikes > 2x baseline, request queue > 500, model load failures rate > 1%
- Immediate steps:
  1. Confirm alert in Grafana and correlation with autoscaler events.
  2. Check recent deploys: `git log --since='1 day' --pretty=oneline` and CI tags.
  3. Run `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` to find OOM/CrashLoop pods.
  4. If GPU saturation: reduce concurrency for non-critical routes: `redwood-cli routes update --concurrency 1 --route /embed`
  5. If model eviction: restart model-manager: `systemctl restart model-manager` (on private) or `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-manager` (hosted)
  6. Engage runtime oncall and escalate to infra if underlying host issues present.
- Diagnostics snippets:
  - PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))`
  - Check cache health: `curl -s http://kv-cache.local/health` -> expect {"status":"ok"}
- Recovery verification:
  - p95 latency returns to <= SLO_target within 15 minutes or continue mitigation.
  - Error rate < 0.1% sustained for 30 minutes.

9) Escalation matrix and communication
- Oncall flow: Primary oncall -> Secondary oncall (15 minutes) -> SRE Lead (30 minutes) -> CTO/Head of Platform (if Sev1 persists > 2 hours)
- Customer comms: Product/CS drafts status updates using the Status Page template. All public statements must be approved by Head of Platform + Legal when PII/data exposure suspected.

10) Continuous improvement and audits
- Quarterly SLO audit: SREs review all service SLOs for accuracy, owner assignment, and label alignment.
- Annual runbook audit: ensure runbooks are up to date, links valid, and playbooks tested via game-days.
- Game-days: runbook drills scheduled bi-annually per team; findings required to be remediated in < 90 days.

Appendices
A. SLO checklist for new service:
1. Define SLI(s) and measurement sources
2. Propose SLO targets and rolling windows
3. Add dashboards and alerts (templates exist in eng-sre/templates)
4. Add runbook and assign oncall
5. Register service in SLO catalog (internal)

B. Runbook template quick copy (Confluence markup)
{panel:title=Runbook template}
h1. {{title}}
h2. Scope & impact
h2. Ownership
h2. Detection
h2. Immediate mitigation steps
h2. Diagnostics
h2. Recovery
h2. Post-incident
{panel}

C. Key links
- SLO catalog: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-catalog
- Runbook templates: /confluence/eng-sre/runbook-templates
- Incident playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

If you are creating or updating an SLO less than the defaults above, please create a justification in the SLO proposal and review with SRE lead and product owner. For questions or help executing capacity calculations, contact eng-sre-capacity@redwood.ai.
